title: 巴西八成家庭背债：分期文化深入骨髓，政府借钱也贵得离谱？
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: Paying for things in installments is deeply ingrained in Brazilian culture.
segments.zh: 分期付款在巴西文化中根深蒂固。

segments.en: If you go to a store, the first thing you're going to hear someone say is budget GBG, which means in how many installments can I pay for this?
segments.zh: 走进商店，首先听到的就是“可以分几期？”

segments.en: You can pay in three installments for installments, five installments and without interest.
segments.zh: 可以分三期、五期，而且免息。

segments.en: But it's only zero interest if you pay on time.
segments.zh: 但只有按时还款才能享受零利率。

segments.en: In a country of massive wealth disparity where tens of millions live below the poverty line, this flexibility has helped make goods more accessible.
segments.zh: 在这个贫富悬殊、数千万人生活在贫困线以下的国家，这种灵活性让商品更易获得。

segments.en: But it can also make it easier to get in over your head.
segments.zh: 但也可能让人更容易陷入债务困境。

segments.en: There are estimates out there that put it at over 80% of households are now holding some type of debt.
segments.zh: 有估计认为，超过80%的家庭目前背负着某种债务。

segments.en: The situation cuts across Latin America's biggest economy and this has political implications.
segments.zh: 这一情况波及拉美最大经济体，并带来政治影响。

segments.en: The election here and the government is definitely worried about the high debt levels.
segments.zh: 选举当前，政府显然对高债务水平感到担忧。

segments.en: If you have an economy in which companies are struggling and families are struggling, you are having a problem ahead in terms of economic growth.
segments.zh: 如果经济中企业和家庭都在挣扎，经济增长就会面临问题。

segments.en: It is a problem that requires attention from whoever becomes president next year.
segments.zh: 无论谁明年成为总统，这个问题都需要关注。

segments.en: After all, even for the government, money is not free.
segments.zh: 毕竟，即使对政府来说，资金也不是免费的。

segments.en: The government, if you want to borrow say 20 years, 30 years, the rates for sky high, the notion that this can go on forever will not survive.
segments.zh: 政府如果想借20年、30年，利率会非常高，这种局面不可能永远持续。
